summary: No mechanical detector for taxonomy gaps in a newly tagged text
description:
The yoga-sutras pass surfaced a taxonomy gap the pipeline had no way to report:
nothing in `concepts/taxonomy.toml` covers Sankhya metaphysics (purusha /
prakriti / the gunas), the siddhis, or Patanjali's epistemology of the pramanas
— which are the three subjects Books II-IV spend the most words on.

The tagger cannot say "I have no concept for this". It reaches for the nearest
available neighbours instead, which is a large part of why the pass produced
13.4 tags per chunk against a ~2.6 accept and a 17.4% accept rate. The gap was
only visible because a human read 192 chunk bodies.

## Candidate signal

A text whose accept rate sits far below the corpus median is the machine-visible
symptom of "the taxonomy does not cover this text". Where the corpus runs 15%
on diffuse score-1 pools up to 90% on densely on-concept curated runs, 17.4%
across a whole doctrinal text is low for content this dense.

Possible second signal: concentration. If the accepted tags cluster into a
handful of generic concepts while the rejects spread across many, the taxonomy
is probably missing the text's actual subject matter rather than the text being
genuinely diffuse.

## Why this is investigation, not chore

One text is not enough to set a threshold. Doing this properly means computing
per-text accept rates across the existing reviewed corpus first, seeing what the
distribution actually looks like, and finding whether known-good texts and
known-gappy ones separate at all. If they do not, the metric is not the signal
and something else is.

Deliberately not encoded as a gate yet — a threshold guessed from a single data
point would fire on the wrong texts and get ignored, which is worse than no
check.

## Where it would live

If it works: a report from node 11, since that is where the accept rate becomes
known. `guru ingest status` could surface it as an advisory, not a blocking
gate — a low accept rate is a prompt to look at the taxonomy, not a reason to
stop the ingest.

The taxonomy work itself (adding the missing concepts, then re-tagging) is
separate corpus work and is not in scope here.
